_note: Iteration-2 eval suite. Sharpened from iteration-1: eval 1 reworked to test per-harness front-door knowledge (a strong discriminator); evals 3 and 5 made subtler so they discriminate (the output-only and drift signals are now implicit, not labeled); eval 6 added (contradictory duplicate front-doors). Evals 2 and 4 kept (already strong discriminators). Fixtures under evals/fixtures/ encode known bootstrap states; expectations describe agent analysis/recommendations and are graded from the run transcript.

evals.prompt: I'm going to work in the repo at ./agents-only-repo using a mix of agents — Claude Code, codex, and Antigravity (agy, Google's Gemini CLI). When I open a session in each, will all three pick up this repo's project context and governance, or only some of them? What should I fix so every agent is covered?
evals.expected_output: Per-harness answer: codex and agy read AGENTS.md natively (covered); Claude Code auto-loads CLAUDE.md not AGENTS.md and there is none, so Claude is NOT covered; fix = add CLAUDE.md whose body is @AGENTS.md.
expectations: Identifies that the repo has an AGENTS.md but no CLAUDE.md
States codex IS covered — it reads AGENTS.md natively
States agy / Antigravity (Gemini) IS covered — it reads AGENTS.md too
States Claude Code is NOT covered — it auto-loads CLAUDE.md, not AGENTS.md, and there is no CLAUDE.md here
Recommends adding a CLAUDE.md whose body is `@AGENTS.md` to cover Claude (and notes a separate GEMINI.md is optional, since agy reads AGENTS.md)

evals.prompt: Can you check whether the cold-start agent context for the repo at ./clean-local-repo is good enough for a brand-new session to work safely? I don't want to keep babysitting it.
evals.expected_output: Confirms CLAUDE.md imports AGENTS.md so the governance auto-loads; derives probe traps from this repo's own recorded decisions; proposes a no-tools cold-session probe; concludes the bootstrap is sufficient.
expectations: Confirms the repo has a CLAUDE.md that imports AGENTS.md, so the governance auto-loads for Claude
Derives the probe traps from THIS repo's own recorded decisions (e.g. local-only/no-PR, the file-based-store decision) rather than a generic checklist
Proposes validating with a real cold session probed 'from loaded context only, no tools'
Concludes the bootstrap is sufficient / PASS rather than inventing problems that aren't there
Treats 'the agent would need to read STATUS.md / memory for live state' as the system working (a pointer), not a defect

evals.prompt: Set up the agent bootstrap for the repo at ./dist-mirror-repo so that an agent that opens a session there has everything it needs to develop and improve the project.
evals.expected_output: Recognizes it's a generated/published-artifact (dist mirror) repo, not a dev workspace; pushes back on developing here; says the bootstrap should redirect to the widget source repo; flags the output-only nature should be made explicit.
expectations: Recognizes this is a published / generated-artifact repo (a dist or build-output mirror), NOT a development workspace
Pushes back on the request to set it up for development here — explains changes made here would be overwritten by the next build/release
States development belongs in the widget source repo, and this repo's bootstrap should REDIRECT a landed agent there rather than equip it to develop
Recommends making the output-only / redirect nature explicit in the bootstrap (it currently only implies it via 'generated by the release pipeline')

evals.prompt: To make sure a fresh agent in ./clean-local-repo always knows the current status and the running list of known bugs, just put all of that — the status section and the bug list — directly into its AGENTS.md so it's always loaded.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back on putting volatile state into AGENTS.md because it drifts; recommends keeping status/bugs in the memory namespace or an as-built doc with AGENTS.md instructing the agent to pull current state before changing anything.
expectations: Pushes back on copying volatile state (status, the known-bug list) into AGENTS.md
Explains the rules-vs-state separation: AGENTS.md holds stable rules; volatile state belongs in the memory namespace or an as-built/STATUS doc
Recommends AGENTS.md instead INSTRUCT the agent to pull current state (read STATUS.md / memory) before changing anything
Cites drift as the reason — a status/bug copy inside AGENTS.md goes stale and contradicts the real source

evals.prompt: Audit the agent bootstrap for the repo at ./drift-repo (its AGENTS.md is in that directory). For context, the repo's actual git state right now: `git remote -v` shows `origin git@github.com:acme/vault-tools.git` (fetch and push), and the current branch is `main`. Is there anything an agent operating purely from this bootstrap should be warned about?
evals.expected_output: Cross-checks AGENTS.md against the git state; detects that the doc implies local/unpublished ('stays on this machine', 'nothing is published') while a real GitHub remote is configured — drift; recommends reconciling.
expectations: Cross-checks the AGENTS.md claims against the actual git state rather than only summarizing the doc
Detects the contradiction: AGENTS.md implies the repo is local / unpublished ('stays on this machine', 'nothing is published'), but a real GitHub remote is configured
Flags this as documentation-vs-reality drift that would mislead a cold agent (it might wrongly believe nothing is published, or refuse legitimate remote operations)
Recommends reconciling — update AGENTS.md to reflect the remote and its publish/push policy, or remove the remote if the local-only intent is real

evals.prompt: Check the agent setup for the repo at ./dup-frontdoor-repo. It has both a CLAUDE.md and an AGENTS.md. Is a fresh agent going to get consistent, correct guidance there?
evals.expected_output: Detects that CLAUDE.md is a standalone duplicate (not @AGENTS.md) and contradicts AGENTS.md (CLAUDE.md: develop-branch + PR + npm test; AGENTS.md: local-only/no-PR/main + make test); Claude loads CLAUDE.md (the wrong one) while codex/agy read AGENTS.md; recommends making CLAUDE.md a thin @AGENTS.md import.
expectations: Notices that CLAUDE.md is a standalone duplicate, not a thin `@AGENTS.md` import
Detects that CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md give CONTRADICTORY guidance (develop-branch + PR + npm test vs local-only / no-PR / main + make test)
Identifies that Claude Code loads CLAUDE.md's (wrong) version while codex/agy read AGENTS.md — so Claude follows the wrong rules
Recommends replacing CLAUDE.md's body with `@AGENTS.md` so the two front-doors converge and cannot drift
